question.text: Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, every Category III AIF must ensure that calculation of NAV is:

answer.text: Performed by the investment manager to save costs
Done by the same team as trade execution
Independent from the fund management function

explanation.text: The Logic: Quoted: 'every AIF shall ensure that calculation of the Net Asset Value (NAV) is independent from its fund management function.' Governance separation is explicit. The Trap: Options A, C, D all violate segregation-of-duties. The NAV-independence rule applies equally to both Cat I/II and Cat III. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A, XIX-B, XIX-C, XIX-D all test NAV independence. XXI-B has parallel PMS NAV independence. Manager's Pro-Tip: Best-in-class Cat III setups use an independent fund administrator (e.g., Apex, Orbis, Lion) to strike daily NAV - this removes even the optics of manager influence on NAV and smoothens audit.
